item.title: The Donation Collector
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Standard SCP pages and test logs

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid dressed in casual street attire, who asks people within a ten foot radius of itself if they would like to make a donation. Anything is a valid donation, and upon receiving the donation, will proceed to put it out of sight before asking whom/what the contributor wishes to be the receiver of the donation. Refusal to donate or acknowledge the entity will result in increasingly aggressive behavior.

Central Narrative: (Attempted) interviews and test logs will be used to tell the story of the article

Hook: I feel like the specifics and the potential of the SCP's abilities are interesting, and there is probably going to be some added gore and spook material added in there as well.

As per the Draft Forum Policies, new authors are to get their concepts reviewed and greenlighted by two experienced reviewers on the Idea Critique Forums before posting on the Draft Critique Forums.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can give assistance in developing an idea before a draft is written. They can also assist in letting you know if something similar exists on the site already, or inform you of various clichés/pitfalls to be cautious of. These elements are more effectively addressed earlier in the writing process.

If you would like to request a draft review without greenlights, you can use the IRC Chatrooms to solicit critique.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note the thread in which you received them, or the users whom provided them.

item.title: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

I find the image of a trans person physically slicing the embodiment of transphobia from themselves to be very powerful, and the final line is basically the closest this thing can have to a happy ending. I'm wondering, do you have any suggestions for making that final paragraph more impactful or obviously important to the metaphor?

The problem here is that making it land better feels like it's…a lot more likely to feel jarring? Really though, my issue is more that the ending feels…not climactic enough? And I'm not sure how to make this feel more climactic tbh without leaning more into the darkness. This said: it might just be my natural inclination towards darker writing that's coming through here rather than an objective truth.

I did consider this, but decided against it as really, these aren't parasites as we understand them but are rather the embodiment of the gender that people feel a trans person should have. Therefore, their ultimate purpose is to totally usurp the host like a cuckoo bird, not to propagate.

Like, I get this and accept your reasoning for this but it feels, to me, a little too loose and up in the air without the propagation; but at the end of the day, this is your call.

I'm not sure how to incorporate it or trim it, although it seems important for thematic purposes that it remain in some form.

It'd work better if there was some additional connection here; where like, -1 is the only one who can affect which way -2 goes but it feels…too much like that'd be putting everything on one person when really it's everyone that affects stuff. Honestly, I don't think it really adds much and I'd just trim it completely if you're not going to e.g. tie it into the end cycle or something instead.

item.title: Re: SCP-XXXX
item.content:encoded:
Well basically, by investigating that room and the house that it is in, they discover that years ago, 7 young girls who had a slumber party there were found dead in the room. The police never found out what happened, but the Foundation suspect another potential SCP to have been responsible. When they died, the room was impregnated with the remnants of the girls' souls with the feeling they had when they died. That's how SCP-XXXX was created. Now, whenever someone enters the room, they are "possessed" by the remnants, and act as previously described. The remnents then behave like some kind of virus, spreading from one person to another through a pillow fight. That's why it could potentially cause the end of the world. If everyone starts running around giggling and pillowfighting forever, human civilization would collapse.

As to how to bring it up, I was thinking of having the Foundation investigate and learn about the 7 girls (as previously stated), then do experiences and talking with one of the possessed one. Then they'll understand that this person is possessed with the remnants of the girls' souls though dialogue.

I know it sounds jarring, but that's why I like it. I love SCPs that are seemingly funny or ridiculous, just to be revealed to actually be dangerous and creepy.

item.title: The Normality
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The most average man in the world, who's everything (height, weight, general routine, you name it) is very normal, has the unconscious power to remove the abnormal properties of every anomaly he comes across temporarily, if not erase it completely, provided that they should remain under his observable range or presence. Doesn't realize his powers, since every anomalous event is forcibly made to look normal to him.

Central Narrative: The Normality was found by accident when one of the SCP broke containment and coincidentally ran into him, henceforth being neutralized and re-secured. At first the foundation takes an interest in him, trying to recruit him since he could be a key to neutralizing all anomaly.

However, none of the foundation members were able to approach him due to his nature, and they decided instead to use him indirectly, by testing and putting forward SCPs to be erased. However, when they planned on erasing a keter class using him, it results in the foundation almost collapsing, since the foundation itself could be considered an anomaly, and anything that could affect his normal life gets influenced by his ability.

After closely preventing that, further testing and attempts to erase anomalies was stopped, because every anomaly he encounters afterwards carries the risk of letting the foundation come under his influence. Hence he was given SCP status, put under watch, and was prevented from coming in contact with anything abnormal.

Hooks: SCP is famous for trying to keep the most anomalous in check. It would interest both new and old fans to see how they would try to deal with the opposite. Also, the foundation's primary goal is to preserve reality and order. The normality could show an outlook on when moving towards that very goal can be disastrous.

Additional notes: This is my first SCP. Please tell me how may I improve on this, if any.

item.title: Re: Misadventures of Bright & Blackwood: Prologue
item.content:encoded:
Summoned by PM.

I'm honestly the wrong person to greenlight this; the Bright List has been called a mistake by its own author, and attempting to integrate that into a semi-serious tale is going to be very difficult. The characterization of "Bright the Chainsaw Cannon-Wielding Maniac" only works in places like r/dankmemesfromsite19, and doesn't really fly on the mainsite anymore, except in deconstructions of that archetype. Plus, I feel like Blackwood and Bright would not get along at all, especially with a characterization of Bright derived from the List, which paints him as a barely-functioning madman who only cares about causing chaos, whereas Blackwood is a refined gentleman adventurer who just happens to be a sea slug.

Bottom line: you're saying that you're going to draw from multiple articles, but you only cite two articles that are 1) the most popular non-SCP articles featuring each of these characters, and 2) fairly shallow looks at both of said characters. If anyone is going to greenlight this, you're going to have to show you're willing to do your research to represent these characters outside of wacky meme hijinks. No Greenlight.

item.title: The Bone Seer
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP document with a large focus on interview/experiment logs

Elevator Pitch: A woman capable of gaining information about others by handling their bones (as well as passing the information on) turns herself in to the Foundation, motivated by a steadfast belief that a K-class scenario is coming.

Central Narrative: After an unrelated incident in which an agent was KIA, the SCP, then working as a mortician, becomes aware of the Foundation via handling the agent's bones and shortly after turns itself in to the Foundation. After the Foundation ensures it's not a GOI agent, the SCP is taken in.

The SCP is able to gain information through physical contact with the bones of others (by what it claims is "listening to the Song") and carve the bones with various occult symbols to allow others to similarly glean the information. It claims its abilities are not born/naturally occurring but rather were taught to it by its grandmother. As the SCP has no living family, the info can not be verified. No attempts to recreate the scrimshaw by using the same symbols or teach others to "listen to the Song" have been successful.

The SCP is motivated by a zealous belief that a K-class scenario is coming soon, though it doesn't know when or how, and the details it describes do not match any known K-class scenarios. It's unclear whether the claim is valid or merely religious - possibly a side effect of the repeated use of its abilities, as it can sometimes have problems distinguishing its own memories from the ones gained via its abilities. This belief does however leave it completely cold and apathetic to individual lives, including its own, as well as highly cooperative with the Foundation, believing it will be necessary to try and piece the world together after the cataclysm.

The Foundation is left trying to find out how reliable is the SCP itself and its claims, as well the extent of its abilities to gain and pass information and whether it could be useful, though it remains wary of possible memetic agents.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reader is left trying to figure out exactly how the SCP works and thinks, how sane it is, and can then turn to the experiment logs to see how various test subjects deal with having the memories of others, sometimes not even human.

Additional Notes: I can provide additional details in comments, but I'm currently at the exact word limit.

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) A Young Reality Disruption
item.content:encoded:
A crit, you say?

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

Overall, I'm not really feeling this. It feels like a forced attempt to try to earn pity points. I'll start with the anomaly first. It boils down to: 'don't hurt me or I'll destroy the world. By accident.'

After this, the Foundation has ordered the agents to lied to the boy's parents that he's going to school abroad.

Why do this when amnestics exist? Or better yet, why not just have the Foundation make up some inventive lie of their own? Maybe fake the humanoid's death. What you've presented gives the parents the possibility that he'll be back. He won't be and even though the Foundation wouldn't tell the parents the truth, they would at least make it known that the humanoid wouldn't be coming back.

SCP-XXXX stated that he discovered his abilities when his father forces him to do a lot of work, which causes him a big amount of stress, also causes him to have a few mental stabilities problem, and sometimes extremely aggressive, he would outburst.

I'd assume the father would at least put two and two together; 'shit hits the fan whenever my son is stressed. Hm.' Unless he's that oblivious.

This is gonna require immense expansion if you choose to pursue this. Something/someone that needs to be tended to and babied with forced attempts at pity points isn't likely to fly.

Being sympathetic towards an unfortunate humanoid has immense possibilities. There are a bunch of humanoid SCPs currently on the site that fit that bill. Think about what makes those SCPs work and try to see if you can find a way to give this old concept a new twist.

Anywho, I apologise if this overly harsh and I do hope I helped. Good day! 👍

item.title: Re: An atavistic humanoid + a mysterious organization
item.content:encoded:
Author, you have 400 words to write out your idea between the pitch, narrative and hook. You're 108 words over the limit.

As for the idea itself… I'm going to have to say no greenlight. You've got two or three different ideas (psychic caveman, mysterious organization that wants to somehow bring back old gods using genetic manipulation, same organization inducing atavism) that don't really gel with one another, on top of other problems.

+ show block
– hide block
  • Why do they need to be psychic? What does it add to the story, other than a compulsion effect? Is this meant to be a sign of some kind of 'divine' aspect, or is it just something humans used to have? If the former, that needs to be made more clear, and if the latter… well, since this SCP deals with evolution, it has to overcome the question of why humans don't have psychic powers today.
  • The idea that a humanoid ancestor had a 'lower IQ' is debatable because 1) IQ is a BS measurement that only really measures your ability to complete puzzles and 2) there are different kinds of intelligence; a Neanderthal would probably have been more naturally intelligent (i.e. more able to be an effective hunter-gatherer) than mathematically intelligent, but that doesn't make them any less smart in that particular field.
  • Evolution is not "always positive", and what qualifies as "positive" is very much relative; for the bacteria that causes staph infections, becoming antibiotic resistant is a very good thing for it, but a very bad thing for us. A lot of parts of evolution are just mutations that don't get bred out for whatever reason; hair color is an example of this.
  • Furthermore, "reverting" evolution is likely not going to be "mostly negative", as evolution adapts to whatever sort of niche that organisms need to fill in that particular epoch. 65 million years ago, theropod dinosaurs were massive things like T. Rex because the niche of a superpredator was appropriate during a time of herbivorous megafauna; as those died out and food became more scarce, nature selected for smaller and smaller theropods that didn't need to eat as much and had the ability to fly, until we're left with everything from kestrels to blue jays in the anthropocene.
  • Finally: evolution in reality is not evolution in Pokemon. If you took the DNA of a Homo sapiens and tried to "revert" it back to a Neanderthal, the closest you could get is attempting to express genes that cause them to resemble Neanderthals; modern human DNA (outside of African peoples) does contain Neanderthal genes, but it is nowhere near enough to revert them back to a Neanderthal, with most humans outside of Africa only possessing 1-2.5% in their genes. If you were attempting to clone a Neanderthal based on existing DNA from remains (which is theoretically possible, as Neanderthal remains still have intact DNA, but very much an ethical quagmire) then it would be a different story.
  • I don't see what correlation exists between "ancient creatures and science" and "speaking Latin".

item.content:encoded:
I'm a 39 year old Community Minister with a philosophy degree and a heavy interest in table top roleplaying games.

A couple of years ago I was volunteering to run roleplaying games at a local high school, and in creating a game setting a couple of the kids mentioning drawing on the SCP setting for influence. When I asked what that was they described it as a collaborative writing project, which I assumed was something they were working on for class. I didn't ask any follow up questions. Six months later I stumbled upon some SCP youtube videos (with some not-really SCP videos, like Sirenhead and creepypastas) and ended up watching quite a few of them, mostly The Volgun and Eastside Show. That's become part of my routine now, when folding laundry or on the treadmill.

I mentioned rpgs as a hobby, but they're also a significant part of my work. I use them extensively in my ministry, as a community building tool and as an educational tool. It was probably inevitable then that I'd end up running a game set in the (well 'an') SCP Universe, and started doing so last Monday. I'm in the process of creating a website for our 'SCP: Outpost 108' campaign. I have a question along those lines; I want to put up some useful intro links, and I was wondering what other people thought should go on that list of links. So far I have a link to each of the following: The SCP Wiki, The SCP Wikipedia page, the wiki glossary page, the wiki security levels page, and the wiki MTF page.

We're not using any of the specific established canons, so this is 'mainline' SCP stuff.

item.title: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
Follow up questions
wow you opened the box

but it feels…like the ending just kinda…happens?

It's important to me for multiple reasons that whatever other changes are made, The nature of the final paragraph remains. I find the image of a trans person physically slicing the embodiment of transphobia from themselves to be very powerful, and the final line is basically the closest this thing can have to a happy ending. I'm wondering, do you have any suggestions for making that final paragraph more impactful or obviously important to the metaphor? I don't want readers to gloss over it by taking it too literally.

it feels, like you'd have this great opportunity for like…the SCP-XXXX instance to crumble into dust and emit more parasites

I did consider this, but decided against it as really, these aren't parasites as we understand them but are rather the embodiment of the gender that people feel a trans person should have. Therefore, their ultimate purpose is to totally usurp the host like a cuckoo bird, not to propagate.

like, the -1 instances really like…come together to crow about how good a job they did protecting their kid from being trans and like, regretting that being trans killed their kid

This is a good idea, but I can't think of a way to do it that isn't too heavy handed or takes away focus from the ending. Further advice would be appreciated.

I'm also kinda iffy about this starting in the mother at all as a thing; it feels…underutilised?

This is very fair. Originally the piece was going to be all about mothers, but as the scope of the metaphor expanded it fell by the wayside. I'm not sure how to incorporate it or trim it, although it seems important for thematic purposes that it remain in some form.

I…am hesitant only in that this feels…miserable?

I am very interested to hear some thoughts about how I could intensify the glimmers of hope that I want to end the piece with.

Thanks for some great crit.

item.title: An atavistic humanoid + a mysterious organization
item.content:encoded:
Edit: Help please! I did something wrong I think.
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: I will tell most of the story trough addenda.

Elevator Pitch:
There is this organization who tries to recreate ancient creatures/gods trough genetic engineering.
When the Foundation attacks one of its labs, they find it to be destroyed, with most of the information taken. Except for one creature. My SCP. The core idea is this:

  • The SCP has treats of our ancestors (relatively low IQ, more hair etc).
  • The SCP can live for 25 years (the less years to live, the more heredity treats).
  • The SCP has the ability to mentally affect other live forms, although it can't do it on command
  • The SCP shows signs of affection towards a junior researcher
+ The story
- close this

The researchers didn't find something abnormal at first, so the security level was relatively low. Then, an attempt to murder the SCP was made. It failed, but the SCP should be contained at a safer location. While in transport to that location, the SCP attacks his guards and walks away. Foundation personal see the SCP, but they aren't alarmed (the third bullet list point, remember?). The SCP walks into the lunch room of the scientific department, and murders senior researcher ''insert name here''. After that, the involved Foundation personal are given a class E status, but are cleared for duty after intensive mental and psychic tests.

+ Reason for my SCP to do that
- I hope this makes sense

Wouldn't it be terrible, not knowing what is real and what is fake? And when you have been fooled so many times that you thought you couldn't be fooled anymore, and then someone you started seeing as a friend betrays you? Well that is what my SCP was thinking. The researcher it murdered was a spy for the organization, as is later discovered by the Foundation (she was the one to try and murder the SCP). My SCP recognized the voice, and thought that it was all just some sort of organization test. It leaves a note saying: ''I believed you'', where he is talking to the junior researcher from bullet list point 4.

Central Narrative:

+ The organization
- G'day! (: 

The idea is that there is an organization that tries to recreate gods/mythological creatures from the past trough genetic engineering. They try to create a leap-back in evolution, otherwise known as an atavism. Evolution is always positive, so reversing it should be mostly negative. That's why most of their attempts fail, or the creature dies at a young age. When the Foundation does an attack on one of its labs, they've already emptied it. Except for one: my SCP. They conduct, just like the Foundation, tests and contain the creatures safely.

+What the Foundation is going to do next 
- Thanks for reading by the way

Since the SCP is the only asset of information about the organization, it should be recovered as soon as possible, and not be killed. The Foundation found a series of text messages on the spy her laptop, talking about killing the SCP. The Foundation needs to find it, before they do.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The discovery of the SCP, that the senior researcher turns out to be a spy, and the relationship between the SCP and the junior researcher.

Additional Notes:
I really need to come up with some names.
Since the organization is about ancient creatures and science, would it make sense for them to speak Latin? I think it does and I can write in it. Let me know please!

item.title: Re: "Magic Horned Dragon"
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback!

I think more mystery could be added to it. Particulary, the idea of an entity being discovered because of a epidemy looks promising but I don't think its original.

I'm definitely going to elaborate on the epidemic part, and try and make it distinct from any other SCPs that may have been discovered that way (not sure if there are any, but still).

Also, if the parasite is able to make the host produces an eletromagnectic pulse wouldnt the infected people also being able to do that? Basically if each infected is capable of producing a EMP, no eletronics would work in a very big area. It could even be a global threat to take the world back to the dark ages depending on how faster the epidemy spreads. The infected are counscious of that? Or they are emmiting an EMP without knowing? A lot of information is missing.

That's actually a good idea, and could justify classification as a Keter. If there was a big enough outbreak, that could cause an (I think it's called an IK-class?) scenario.

You have some key elements here that you have to tie together: the creature, the parasite, the epidemy and the eletromagnectic pulse. What is the creature? It has a reason to look like that? If the parasite is able to preserve tissue to survive inside the creature like its alive, it could REALLY be a Prolibytherium. It could make the host emit a EMP because eletricity could be a danger to him, etc, etc.

I hadn't considered that the parasite may be causing the main SCP to function like that. I merely had it as the Prolibytherium being able to do that of its own accord, and simply transporting the parasites (which have a greatly-accelerated growth rate). That's a good suggestion, though.

Thanks again!

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) A Young Reality Disruption
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid male that would accidentally warp-reality if he has too much stress or gets intensely outrageous.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX is a reality-altering humanoid male that is approximately 2 feet tall. The subject will accidentally disrupt reality if mental capacities are large, resulting in a ZK-Class event occur. Their unstable emotions are the sources that can affect their power's capabilities, efficacy, and limitations.

SCP-XXXX was discovered when reports of a paranormal event have occurred, which is shown to be various vehicles falling from the skies, killing thousands of innocent lives. After this was brought to the Foundation, they've located all of the scene witnesses and wipe out their memories. Before doing so, they've asked the witnesses whether they know the cause of the phenomena. The civilians all said that they have no clue what the cause could be. The agents all know that who, or whatever could do so, is somewhere around in that area, as they've asked each people in the area until they've moved to the house of a high school male, which eventually claims that he is the cause of the phenomenon. After this, the Foundation has ordered the agents to lied to the boy's parents that he's going to school abroad.

In the interview, SCP-XXXX stated that he discovered his abilities when his father forces him to do a lot of work, which causes him a big amount of stress, also causes him to have a few mental stabilities problem1, and sometimes extremely aggressive, he would outburst.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: The high-school is a person who lives in a family with a very rigorous father. Due to seeing his son being too joyful and doesn't seem to care whether if he gets in trouble, the father always scolds him non-stop, slowly affecting his mental health.

Additional Notes:

Footnotes
1. Stated that he sometimes talks alone, play with his pencil, walks, run, and jumps around in circles while pulling his hair and talking alone at the same time.
